extracted.intended_audience: United Way staff, partner designers, marketers, communicators, and external vendors producing branded materials
extracted.subtask_description: Visual identity and brand guidelines for using United Way logos, colors, typography, photography, graphic elements, iconography, and data visualization across communications and channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual identity toolkit usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The toolkit includes logo, color palette, typography, graphic elements, photography, iconography and data visualization styles; when applied together these elements can be modulated across regions, audiences, channels and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the elements together to convey the brand; modulate (adapt) elements appropriately by region/audience/channel while maintaining overall brand coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo symbol integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The logo symbol (Circle of Hope) should always appear in its entirety and never be deconstructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not separate, remove, or alter parts of the symbol; maintain the rainbow, hand support and person elements intact to preserve personality and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logotype and logo structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Logotype is refreshed and the logo symbol and logotype have been removed from the rectangular holding shape to convey an open, inclusive, dynamic approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the updated logotype and structure as provided; the logo has been optimized for small spaces and digital media. See Localization subsection for localized use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred logo arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizontal logo is the preferred version; vertical logo is suitable for vertical layouts to optimize space and legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use horizontal where possible; use vertical only when layout or legibility benefits (vertical layouts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full logo vs symbol usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The full logo should be used in all contexts, except for small spaces (e.g., favicon or social media icon) where the logo symbol may be used on its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer full logo for most applications; in constrained contexts use symbol-only. Refer to Logo Variations and small-space guidance for alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo clear space
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the logo clear of competing text, images and graphics by maintaining a minimum amount of clear space equal to the height of 'U' of the logo on all sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and maintain that minimum clear space on every side in every application; do not allow other elements to encroach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo minimum sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum sizes to keep logo legible: horizontal logo widths equal to or greater than 2.0” for print and 200 px for digital; vertical logo widths equal to or greater than 1.0” for print and 100 px for digital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never display logo smaller than these dimensions; for very small merchandise ensure minimum size still met or use symbol-only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-space logo applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In small merchandise or limited canvas applications, ensure the logo meets minimum size requirements and maintain clear space rules; if additional text is required alongside the logo, preserve clear space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided examples as patterns for small-space layouts; prioritize legibility over decorative placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web and social icon usage
rubrics_metrics.description: For web and social media use the logo symbol to represent the brand; follow platform minimum sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform minimums listed: X/Twitter 400x400 px, Facebook 200x200 px, Instagram 150x150 px, LinkedIn 400x400 px, YouTube 800x800 px. Favicon minimum 16x16 px.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo color and alteration prohibitions (Logo Don'ts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The logo is the most recognizable representation of our brand and must not be altered under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rotate; change colors; crop; skew, distort or stretch; reconfigure or change logo elements; add artistic effects; use translucency; integrate the logo into messaging (replace letters); or use the logo as copy inside a sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo variations and contrast rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Full-color version is preferred. Knockout (white) for dark backgrounds or photos; one-color (black) for grayscale or one-color printing. The United Way logotype is blue unless contrast requires white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not adjust the logo symbol colors. Ensure sufficient contrast for clarity and legibility when used over photography or backgrounds; choose appropriate variation per background contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the logo over photography
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sufficient contrast between background photography and logo for optimal clarity and legibility; if photo is busy or low contrast, use a gradient between photo and logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended steps: place photo, add a gradient set to Multiply blending mode, add logo in a section with enough contrast. Always test legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary color palette and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary colors are blue, red and yellow (derived from logo) each with four shades; preferred shades correspond to logo. Primary colors (one, two or all three) should be applied across communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use primary colors as dominant across core communications. Tones can add texture/depth but should not replace primary colors. Refer to Bringing the Elements to Life for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary and tertiary color roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary color is green; tertiary colors are purple and black. Use secondary/tertiary colors in a supporting role, not as the main or dominant color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply secondary/tertiary as accents or in data visualization; do not let them take precedence over primary colors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color accessibility and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved color combinations meet WCAG 2.1 level AA contrast ratios; ensure sufficient contrast for visibility and legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing typography and background colors, check contrast ratios using tools (e.g., Adobe Color Contrast Analyzer). Use combinations provided that meet AA standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color application rule (primary dominance)
rubrics_metrics.description: All core communications should prominently feature at least one, but preferably all three, primary colors as the dominant color(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use primary colors as focal point; complement with secondary/tertiary accents and tones to add energy/depth without detracting from the primary palette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand fonts and fallbacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Antonio is brand font for headlines (all-uppercase); Palanquin is brand font for body copy; Noto is alternate where Antonio/Palanquin unavailable; Arial is the default system font; Monte Carlo Script reserved for special events/collateral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download fonts from Google Fonts as directed. Use alternate fonts only where primary fonts are unavailable. Reserve Monte Carlo Script for sophisticated event materials (e.g., fundraising gala).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography usage and hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Typography and color should create clear messaging hierarchy. Italics are not recommended (they appear disruptive with Antonio); if necessary, use italics of the alternate brand font (Noto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Antonio for bold headlines and Palanquin for body to maintain hierarchy and legibility. Avoid italics unless using Noto italics as exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography style and authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Photography should be community-rooted, responsive, highlight people in action, and express the brand promise — engaging, energizing and elevating; AI-generated photography and people-based illustrations should never be used as a substitute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select images that showcase people connecting to their community. Prioritize trust and transparency; avoid staged/inauthentic imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography don'ts
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid photos that are out of focus; with unnatural/extreme filters or effects; overly posed; on blank backgrounds/silhouetted and lacking context; low resolution or poor quality; overly busy or complex composition; AI-generated or people-based illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add captions when necessary (left-aligned below photo). Always prioritize clarity, context, and authenticity in image selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic elements purpose and inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic elements (arc, arrow, circle) are inspired by the logo symbol and should be used to advance brand strategy and story — connective, responsive and scalable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use elements to reinforce brand promise and personality; they are strategic tools, not decoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic elements configuration and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize the circle and arc as heroic components; use the arrow as a supportive element to signal points of impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply elements in connective (overlapping arrangements), responsive (dynamic arrangements to evoke movement), or scalable (ripple effect) ways to reflect comprehensive, solution-oriented, cascading impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic elements don'ts
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use graphic elements decoratively or in ways that confuse the brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific prohibitions: no bullseye (innermost circle too small); do not use multiple graphic element styles at once; no polka dots (decorative compositions); no chevron or alternative arrow shapes; no mosaics of multiple graphic elements; no uneven line art — use clean orbits only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconography style and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Icons are a simple line treatment with rounded edges (mirroring the logo's radiating lines) and have an opening to inspire audiences to learn more; icons serve functional purposes (navigation, comprehension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize icons for legibility and clarity in small spaces. Icons may be rendered in any primary color, but an icon set should ideally be displayed in the same primary color. Ensure proper contrast with background. Locate provided icon sets in Brandfolder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data visualization style and color usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Data visualization employs rounded edges and color blocks to complement the logo and create a vibrant representation of impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible use primary colors to emphasize the largest or most important data points; use secondary/tertiary colors for smaller or less important data.
